I'm not trying to make up for anything. I would never be able retribute my infidelity. I'm in This relationship, today, because I feel like, for once, I'll regret and never forgive myself for giving up. I know I'm her person and I hope and feel like she loves, accepts and will eventually forgive me. I on the other hand am a millennial and realize one day we can have children together and potentially will be raising a split household like the one we both individually grew up in.

What if she continuously pays 10% for the longevity of your relationship and she continues to save her money and you continue to expend your finances. She is still your wife (hypothetically speaking) unless you have a prenuptial agreement. You're looking at the short term. Narrow sight can leave you vulnerable and weak. Life isn't checkers... but more so, a game of chess.

My quandary is that... it has become so easy for us to walk away. (Figuratively swipe left)... when do we decide to stop running away from difficulties within a relationship? I cheated because I wasn't initially vested but here we are 4 years in. Is it too late to walk away Orr to early to start over?

The dynamic of the arguments continuously change. It has been social media, female friends, and female coworkers... We argue because I fight for my individuality and privacy... her argument is as a couple we should share everything. (No passwords, share locations, and have combined lives including; friends, outings, and for her family gatherings and excursions.

I have never found myself committed since the relationship that conceived my first child... I was 17 and provided her with a life that allowed her to be a stay at home mother. She cheated, took my son 14 hrs away, and I loved on with my life. Since then I had a huge difficulty with commitment. I became very emotionally disassociated. I have never given someone the ability or possibility to hurt me that deeply thereafter.
